**Round 361 = PERF-10b-i: the active track moves into the selection store**
- **Problem:** clicking a clip on another lane re-rendered 83 components; a click on the same lane re-renders 15. The cause is that the active lane is stored in the shared app state, so every change re-renders everything that reads it.
- **Change:** the active lane joins the existing selection store, so no new store is added. Only the two affected lanes, the library's "Active track" line and the collapsed-group highlight now update. Nothing changes on screen.
- **What I ran on a scratch copy before writing the task:**
  - Typecheck passes, and lint shows 205 warnings, the same as HEAD.
  - The full test suite passes: 3643 tests, plus four new ones (SS8–SS11).
  - The production perf run passes 95/95 budget checks, with no new rows. A cross-lane click drops from **83 to 42** components, with identical samples at normal speed and 6× CPU slowdown.
- **Proof the checks can fail:** I made seven deliberate breakages (MU-1…MU-7). Each one makes exactly the check it targets fail. MU-7 is the proof for the new commit-count limit.
- **Browser baseline:** I ran the three new browser checks on HEAD (which lane is active, the collapsed-group highlight, paste onto the active lane) and saved the values C will compare against.
- **Budgets:** two click rows switch from recorded to enforced limits: at most 42 components and at most 2 commits.
